experiment: M2.1 PART B: multi-seed replication of the incident-level leakage causal test (experiments/results/incident_leakage_audit.json's Part D), checking whether the committed single-seed +0.2433 accuracy gap is stable across the balancing draw
finding: Across 3 seeds, mean Delta_acc = +0.2416 (std 0.0022) against the committed single-seed +0.2433. Mean is within +/-0.01 and std is below 0.005: the leakage effect is a stable property of the balancing draw, not an artefact of seed 42.

per_seed.design: Both buckets are drawn from GUIDE_train.csv rows past the 100,000-row training slice, so the model trained on neither. 'leaked' rows belong to an incident that does appear in the training slice (a labelled sibling was available); 'clean' rows do not. Both are class-balanced to identical per-class counts.

accuracy_bootstrap_ci.method: percentile bootstrap, resampling paired (y_true, y_pred) rows with replacement
percentile bootstrap, resampling paired (y_true, y_pred) rows with replacement

accuracy_gap_leaked_minus_clean.method: percentile bootstrap on the difference between two independently-resampled samples (not a paired/McNemar comparison -- a and b are different alerts)
accuracy_gap_leaked_minus_clean.interpretation: metric(a)-metric(b) = +0.2433, 95% CI [+0.2282, +0.2587]. This excludes 0, so the gap is a real effect at this sample size, not sampling noise.
